title: Robertson panel directive to watch and infiltrate UFO groups

tellings.quote: and and again from the Robertson panel too the the directive was um let's keep an eye on UFO act uh groups

tellings.page: Part II, Unofficial Investigating Groups, pp. 1416-1417
tellings.quote: It was believed that such organizations should be watched because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking if widespread sightings should occur. The apparent irresponsibility and the possible use of such groups for subversive purposes should be kept in mind.

plain: A 1953 panel convened by the CIA, the US government's foreign intelligence agency, is said to have directed the government to watch, and perhaps get inside, civilian groups that investigated UFOs. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, tells Michels that the directive from this panel, known as the Robertson Panel, was "let's keep an eye on UFO groups." The other telling is the panel's own report, written by the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence and dated 16 February 1953. It names two civilian groups, the "Civilian Flying Saucer Investigators" in Los Angeles and the "Aerial Phenomena Research Organization" in Wisconsin. It says such organizations "should be watched because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking if widespread sightings should occur," and that "the possible use of such groups for subversive purposes should be kept in mind." That matches what Salas describes as keeping an eye on them. Whether watching meant infiltrating, as the story's name has it, the report neither says nor rules out. If it went that far, the very groups trying to study UFOs would have been under quiet government watch from early on.

discussion.by: Report of Meetings of Scientific Advisory Panel on Unidentified Flying Objects (Robertson Panel), 14-18 January 1953
discussion.text: The panel's minutes name the "Civilian Flying Saucer Investigators" and the "Aerial Phenomena Research Organization" and say such organizations "should be watched because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking" and that "the possible use of such groups for subversive purposes should be kept in mind", an official recommendation to keep watch on named civilian groups, which is what Salas tells as "keep an eye on". The step from watched to infiltrated, which the story's name carries, is a reading the report as released neither confirms nor excludes. As context, not as evidence: how a watch was to be kept is the kind of thing such minutes rarely set down.
